questions.q: What, according to the article, are the rites of Hajj – the circuits, the run between Safa and Marwah, the sacrifice?
options: A symbolic re-enactment of stages in the life of Prophet Abraham and his family
Yes. “It is a tradition of your father, Abraham.”
Rules laid down by later scholars
Not quite. The article says: A symbolic re-enactment of stages in the life of Prophet Abraham and his family.
Exercises to prepare pilgrims for travel
Not quite. The article says: A symbolic re-enactment of stages in the life of Prophet Abraham and his family.
Customs taken over from the traders of Makkah
Not quite. The article says: A symbolic re-enactment of stages in the life of Prophet Abraham and his family.
questions.rationale: “The rituals of Hajj are a symbolic re-enactment of the various stages of the life of the Prophet Abraham… so that the believer repeats the lessons from this history in his own life.”

questions.q: Besides memorising prayers and rules, what does the article say will make a pilgrim’s Hajj “a living Hajj”?
options: Staying longer in Makkah
Not quite. The article says: Knowing the history that runs from Hajira and Ishmael to the Prophet and his Companions.
Knowing the history that runs from Hajira and Ishmael to the Prophet and his Companions
Right. Then the rites become a deep spiritual experience.
Travelling with a large group
Not quite. The article says: Knowing the history that runs from Hajira and Ishmael to the Prophet and his Companions.
Performing Hajj several times
Not quite. The article says: Knowing the history that runs from Hajira and Ishmael to the Prophet and his Companions.
questions.rationale: “If pilgrims read this history, they will know the historical background of the worship they perform. In this way, their Hajj will become a living Hajj.”

questions.q: Astronomers have found a black hole heavy enough to swallow the solar system. How does the article say a thoughtful person should receive such discoveries?
options: As a reason to fear the future
Not quite. The article says: As a means of realising God’s greatness and his own helplessness.
As a means of realising God’s greatness and his own helplessness
Yes. Science has “enlarged the canvas of God realization.”
As proof that the universe has no order
Not quite. The article says: As a means of realising God’s greatness and his own helplessness.
As matters for specialists only
Not quite. The article says: As a means of realising God’s greatness and his own helplessness.
questions.rationale: “These facts remind man of his state of extreme helplessness and the state of Omnipotence of God.”

questions.q: Who are the true believers, in the article’s description?
options: Those who bow to truth on the strength of argument, while nothing compels them
Correct. In the Hereafter, belief will no longer be a choice.
Those who never ask for reasons
Not quite. The article says: Those who bow to truth on the strength of argument, while nothing compels them.
Those who are born into a believing family
Not quite. The article says: Those who bow to truth on the strength of argument, while nothing compels them.
Those who believe once they see God’s power
Not quite. The article says: Those who bow to truth on the strength of argument, while nothing compels them.
questions.rationale: “The true believers are those who believe in God on the basis of argument, who bow to truth while there is no other incentive at work.”

questions.article: The ‘islamic State of Is’ Is Not an Islamic State
questions.q: How, according to the article, did Abu Bakr become head of the community after the Prophet’s death?
options: By inheriting the position
Not quite. The article says: Through open consultation and the consensus of the Companions.
By declaring himself caliph
Not quite. The article says: Through open consultation and the consensus of the Companions.
Through open consultation and the consensus of the Companions
Yes. No one may proclaim himself ruler.
By the support of the army
Not quite. The article says: Through open consultation and the consensus of the Companions.
questions.rationale: “Open consultation took place between the Companions. Through the consensus of the Companions, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq became the head of the state of Madinah.”

questions.q: The article speaks of “extracting” spiritual food from material things, with a glass of water as the example. What does it mean?
options: Reflecting on how fitly a thing serves us until it leads to appreciation of God’s wisdom
Well reasoned. “Man cannot live by bread alone.”
Eating and drinking very little
Not quite. The article says: Reflecting on how fitly a thing serves us until it leads to appreciation of God’s wisdom.
Studying the chemistry of what we consume
Not quite. The article says: Reflecting on how fitly a thing serves us until it leads to appreciation of God’s wisdom.
Blessing food and drink before taking them
Not quite. The article says: Reflecting on how fitly a thing serves us until it leads to appreciation of God’s wisdom.
questions.rationale: “You have to develop your mind to such an extent that you are able to extract the spiritual content from material things.”

questions.q: Which lesson of Hajj does the article single out when it speaks of people of many languages and cultures performing the rites together?
options: That the pilgrimage should be made easier
Not quite. The article says: Living together as one community in spite of differences, and a sense of human equality.
That one language should replace the others
Not quite. The article says: Living together as one community in spite of differences, and a sense of human equality.
That travel broadens the mind
Not quite. The article says: Living together as one community in spite of differences, and a sense of human equality.
Living together as one community in spite of differences, and a sense of human equality
Right. It is “a complete course of life’s training.”
questions.rationale: “Hajj is a great training course which, despite differences and disagreements, teaches us to live together as one community.”

questions.q: Why, says the article, are people so ready to believe ill of those who have risen to prominence?
options: Because the truth is hard to find out
Not quite. The article says: Because of jealousy – a reluctance to accept another’s superiority.
Because of jealousy – a reluctance to accept another’s superiority
Yes. This was Satan’s fault towards Adam.
Because people love justice
Not quite. The article says: Because of jealousy – a reluctance to accept another’s superiority.
Because prominent people are usually guilty
Not quite. The article says: Because of jealousy – a reluctance to accept another’s superiority.
questions.rationale: “Man’s greatest weakness is his reluctance to accept the superiority of another.”

questions.q: What lesson does the article draw from the story of the Prophet Ayyub (Job)?
options: Suffering is always a punishment
Not quite. The article says: No loss in this world is final; with patience and hope in God one may recover and gain more.
No loss in this world is final; with patience and hope in God one may recover and gain more
Exactly. His family and wealth were restored twice over.
Wealth is a danger to faith
Not quite. The article says: No loss in this world is final; with patience and hope in God one may recover and gain more.
One should not own many possessions
Not quite. The article says: No loss in this world is final; with patience and hope in God one may recover and gain more.
questions.rationale: “God… has devised the system of this world in such a way that here no loss or deprival is final.”

questions.q: “If you put the cart before the horse, you will never reach your destination.” In the article, which is the horse and which the cart?
options: Rights come first; duties follow
Not quite. The article says: Peace comes first; justice and rights are worked for through the opportunities peace opens.
Justice comes first; peace follows from it
Not quite. The article says: Peace comes first; justice and rights are worked for through the opportunities peace opens.
Wishes come first; plans follow
Not quite. The article says: Peace comes first; justice and rights are worked for through the opportunities peace opens.
Peace comes first; justice and rights are worked for through the opportunities peace opens
Yes. This is presented as a law of nature.
questions.rationale: “One must try to establish peace at any cost… Peace will then open the doors of opportunities. And, by availing these opportunities, one should work towards achieving justice.”
